purpose: Whole-character 24-frame visual trial; not approved animation
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: true full-character frame-by-frame animation sprite sheet, not skeletal parts, not a pose collection.
Reference image 1 is the approved character identity. Match that whole puppy exactly: apricot coat, cream forehead blaze/muzzle/chest/socks, brown drooping ears, forest sage collar and small round brass tag, chocolate outlines, gentle cel shading, cute natural quadruped puppy proportions. DO NOT copy any humanoid hand or chin-resting gesture. All four dog paws stay naturally on the ground.

Produce exactly TWENTY-FOUR consecutive FULL-BODY animation frames in one precisely regular SIX-column by FOUR-row atlas, landscape 3:2 aspect ratio, ideally 1536x1024 so each square cell is 256x256. Read frames from left to right, then next row. Every cell has exactly one complete puppy, comfortably centered on an identical ground baseline at 89% of its cell height. Fixed camera, same body scale, same paw positions, same torso and haunch anatomy, same head size, same color patches and outline weight in all 24 frames. Keep at least 8% clear transparent margin on every side of every frame. Entire background genuinely transparent. No grid, borders, labels, frame numbers, props, symbols, text, drop shadow or checkerboard pixels.

Animate ONE seamless two-second attentive seated cycle with 24 genuine small in-between drawings, each 1/12 second apart:
Frames 1-6: neutral sitting puppy gradually tilts its head about 10 degrees toward viewer's right. Its neck and chest connect naturally in every drawing. The near ear follows the tilt with a little lag. No body lean.
Frames 7-12: the head gently returns to neutral. Eyes go half-closed in frame 10, closed in 11, half-open in 12.
Frames 13-18: head gently tilts about 7 degrees toward viewer's left with alert open eyes. Ears follow naturally, head size unchanged.
Frames 19-24: smoothly return toward neutral. Last frame leads into first frame without a snap. Frame24 is immediately before frame1, not a duplicated hold.
Across the whole cycle the tail is genuinely redrawn wagging left/right in a subtle soft arc, 3 tail-wag cycles over 24 frames, with continuous curvature and visible changes; no detached rigid rotated tail. The feet, hindquarters, collar and main torso stay registered, with only tiny natural breathing. Neck connection is always complete. Every frame is a complete anatomical drawing, no separate pasted parts. No stretching limbs, no extra toes or legs, no floating neck, no different dog per cell. Smooth incremental changes rather than 24 unrelated dramatic poses.
This is a conservative polished game sprite animation: preserve character identity and anatomical drawing quality above exaggerated action. Do not generate separate parts or an exploded rig.
